a:r.a:t: Tumor cells often grow faster than angiogenesis allows growth of capillaries to aerate them, resulting in anaerobic metabolism.
Tumor cells increased expression of LDH.
Compounds that inhibit key steps in glycolysis can kill cancer cells by limiting energy production.

p:cNvPr.descr: An image depicting the anaerobic metabolism of glucose in tumor cells. At the top is an arrow pointing down to glucose in a tan box. To the right of the arrow is glucose uptake. To the left is GLUT1 and GLUT 3, both in blue. To the left of each of these is a green arrow pointing up. Below glucose is an arrow pointing down to glucose 6-phosphate in a tan box. To the left of the arrow is hexokinase in blue. To the left of that is a green arrow pointing up. To the left of this and the two green arrows above is cancer. There is a dashed arrow from cancer going up and right to the green arrows, and down and right to the green arrow. To the right of the arrow is 2-deoxyglucose with a dashed arrow pointing to the left to a red X in a red circle. Below this is lonidamine pointing left with a dashed arrow to a red X in a circle. Below that is 3-bromopyruvate with an arrow pointing left with a dashed arrow to a red X in a circle. Glucose 6-phosphate has an arrow pointing right to 6-phosphogluconate in a tan box. Above the arrow is 6-amino nicotinic acid with a dashed arrow pointing down to a red X in a circle. Below the arrow is glucose 6-phosphate dehydrogenase in blue. 6-phosphogluconate points down to xylulose 5-phosphate in a tan box, which has an arrow pointing left to glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate in a tan box. Above the arrow is oxythiamine, which has a dashed arrow pointing down to a red X in a circle. Below the arrow is transketolase in blue. Glucose 6-phosphate also has a dashed arrow pointing down to the glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate. A dashed arrow below glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate points down to pyruvate in a tan box. Glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate also has a solid arrow pointing down, then right to 2 ATP/glucose in a pink box. Pyruvate has an arrow pointing up, then right to 2 ATP/glucose in the red box. Pyruvate has an arrow to the right pointing right, then branching up through aerobic respiration to [wavy line]30 ATP/glucose. Above this line is hypoxia pointing down to a red X in a circle with a dashed arrow. The other arrow points down to 3CO2. In the backgrounds is an image of aerobic respiration with mitochondrion around the outer edges. To the right is cancer (p53) and a dashed arrow left to a red X in a circle on the right edge of the figure. To the left, there is a bracket that extends from the glucose 6-phosphate down to pyruvate. To the left of the bracket is hypoxia. Below that is a dashed arrow pointing down to HIF-1. To the left of this is a green arrow pointing up. Below this is a dashed arrow pointing down to glycolytic enzymes. To the left of this is a green arrow pointing up.
